messages.content: What kind of fertilizer is best for growing tomatoes?

function.name: soil_analysis_analyze_soil_type
function.description: Analyze a type of soil and provides characteristics about it. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

soil_type.description: The type of the soil. For example, loam, sandy, etc.

parameters_needed.description: Optional specific characteristics of the soil to analyze.

message.content: The best fertilizer for tomatoes depends on your soil’s current nutrient levels, but generally a balanced NPK mix (like 10-10-10) works well. If your soil is low in nitrogen, use a higher N fertilizer (e.g., 15-5-10). If it’s deficient in potassium or phosphorus, adjust accordingly. A slow‑release granular fertilizer applied at planting and again when fruit starts forming is ideal. Organic options like composted manure or fish emulsion also boost overall soil health and provide a steady nutrient supply.
